liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Rollin' & Tumblin'** (2 other sources): First time the Dead played this song live, per the notes; Notes mark it as the first time the band played it [1][6]
- **Touch Of Grey** (1 review): A person flew over the stage during the opener, which the reviewer remembers fondly [16]
- **Ramble On Rose** (1 review): Reviewer calls this one decent, among a few musical bright spots in an otherwise weak show [18]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): Singled out as one of the good performances of the night [19]
- **Standing On the Moon** (1 review): Singled out, with Samba and Standing On the Moon, as good performances [19]

## Setlist highlights

- **Rollin' & Tumblin'**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [22]

## The recordings

- **gd1995-06-15.135288.aud.fob.lamarre-berger.flac1648** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 156 min [1]
- **gd95-06-15.schoeps.7745.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 163 min; rated 2.77/5 by 60 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the audience recording's sound quality quite good [15]
- **gd1995-06-15.145838.sony.ecm909a.sterry.beckwith.miller.sirmick.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 157 min [5]. Said about its sound: Left channel dropped out in this song; the right channel was copied over, making it mono; Many static-like noises in the left channel were mostly removed; Set II start levels were corrected [5]
- **gd1995-06-15.143132.SonyECM-909A.sterry.beckwith.sirmick.miller.flac2496**: source not stated; 20 songs; 157 min [6]. Said about its sound: First two Set II tracks may come from a different source; Promised Land has a left dropout [6]

## Around the show

- A local listener attended in their hometown and hung a 'Camping Here' sign for friends in the Highgate fields [10]
- Jerry missed lyrics despite a teleprompter; the camping and partying outside were enjoyable [12]
- Listener drove nonstop from St. George, Utah, partied all night, and got in free [13]
- Residents of the small, hot Vermont town were kind, the crowd danced, and this listener paid for a ticket without gate-crashing [15]
- Reached the stage after walking about three miles; the crowd near the stage was extremely tight [16]
- Dylan's opening set was pretty good; Jerry stumbled through the Dead's show [17]
- Bands played from trucks in the parking lot; reviewer claims TC played with a band called Yep [17]
- The walk into the fairgrounds was dusty and trashy; a large security guard chased the reviewer for urinating outdoors [18]
- Reviewer saw this as the start of the troubled summer 1995 tour, with the band seeming near the end [16]
- Not an awesome show, but better than many other 1995 shows; audience recording sounds great [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1995-06-15.135288.aud.fob.lamarre-berger.flac1648**: taped by Doug Lamarre; transferred by Rob Berger; source: flac16/48kHz ; source: FOB daud master taped by Doug Lamarre; Sanken COS-11BP lavalier mics (Dan Liff’s r.i.p.) > Denon DTR-80P 30’ in front of soundboard;… [1]
- **gd95-06-15.schoeps.7745.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Matt Bertollo and Tim Wiley; source: Audience: Schoeps MK4V's [2]
- **gd1995-06-15.145838.sony.ecm909a.sterry.beckwith.miller.sirmick.flac16**: taped by George Sterry; transferred by Charlie Miller and SIRMick and David Beckwith; source: Source: Sony ECM-909A > Sony WM-D3 > Cassette Master (Maxell XL-II90) - Recorded by George Sterry * [5]
- **gd1995-06-15.143132.SonyECM-909A.sterry.beckwith.sirmick.miller.flac2496**: taped by George Sterry; transferred by Charlie Miller and SIRMick and David Beckwith; source: Sony ECM-909A > Sony WM-D3 > Cassette Master (Maxell XL-II90) - Recorded by George Sterry [6]
